So, today I went about business as usual (mostly). After a long hard night of editing, I uploaded the latest episode of my game news show to Youtube- however, today I couldn't stick around to make sure everything worked fine- today, I had to be away from my computer and it wasn't until I returned home that I noticed my episode had no views. It seemed peculiar until I logged into Youtube with my other account and- ah. There it was.

The video was blocked worldwide, courtesy of a copyright claim from the BBC. As fate would have it, I talked about the upcoming Lego Dimensions- this week, they unveiled that Doctor Who would be part of the game. So, I used the new Lego Dimensions trailer with the Lego Doctor and TARDIS and all that- and apparently, that was the issue. The trailer uses music from Doctor Who. That, apparently, triggered the Copyright Enforcement Automated Sentinel Excisors (the CEASE, I'm still waiting for the DESIST to come in the mail) and as a result, nobody (except, perhaps, the people who see my show on television in Georgia) got to watch this week's episode.

I filed a dispute and had the video restored, but this cost me a day of views.

What's especially upsetting, however, is that there was no warning that my video had been automatically flagged and blocked- no notification from the Google Plus integration they so mercifully shoved down everybody's throat, no bar at the top of the page mentioning that I'm the only one who can watch the video, not even a notice on the video itself. I got an email about it, but beyond that? Nothing. The system is badly implemented and causes trouble aplenty.

How would you fix the system?
Youtube's automated copyright system just caused me a bunch of trouble. How can it be fixed?

As far as your situation goes, It's not the end of the world. These things happen all the time. Technically you should be safe under fair use because you are doing a produced news show, but these things always come up eventually. I'm sure majority of gamers get a blocked video at some point. Just be careful to avoid a copyright strike.

As far as content id goes: The system is there to protect the people in control: google and the companies that originally created the media. It's not very accurate for detecting legit produced videos under fair use. However people forget that this little barrier is what prevents companies from coming directly to you for potential copyright lawsuits. If youtube didn't exist and everyone had to have their own video platform it would be chaos. It would be like the legal battle against bittorrent. Since their is no authority for bittorrent, the blame goes everywhere and everyone is held at fault.

If I was in your position I would either not use any copyrighted material or not cover any products from copyright holders that hit you with DCMA complaints. If you feel a copyright holder is being unfair you should not cover there products any more. Why give BBC any promotion for a game when they will punish you for trying to help promote it. I know some channels that refuse to play any music not provided by youtube for content creators.

A large part of this issue is caused by the way DCMA is written. Google does not want to spend money to fight a battle against copyright holders. The copyright holders have an insane amount of power and the only way to change there mind is to effect the amount of money they make.

The system in question is ContentID. It's almost completely automated, which when you consider the number of new videos uploaded to YouTube every day, is pretty much necessary. Still, they could throw a few more warm bodies at it, and try to reduce the number of really terrible actions, like artists having their own work, released by their own label, blocked. Yes, this does happen. Read TechDirt.
We need a better alternative to youtube.

My old friend Dan was coming to visit. Dan was the Best Man at our wedding four years ago, and soon after the wedding he had taken a job out of State. I had visited him two years ago, and now he was coming to town to spend the weekend with us. Dan and my wife, Joanne, had only met during our courtship but had a real chemistry with each other. I'm reasonably sure that had I not been in the picture that those two would have been a real item.

After a long day's drive Dan arrived late afternoon Friday and it became an immediate happy hour. We spent a couple hours catching up and having drinks. I asked Dan about his love life and he told us that it was nowhere, between his work and his poor luck in choosing dates it had been six months since he had even been out with a women.

He said that knowing Joanne has spoiled him and that maybe he was setting his bar too high. This brought a sigh and a long hug from Joanne. After the hug Dan looked Joanne in the eye and said, beautiful, smart and sexy. At this Joanne flushed and hugged him again.

After having several drinks none of us felt it was safe to drive anywhere, so we ordered dinner in and continued the celebration. Joanne is not much of a drinker and I could tell she had a pretty good buzz going, as she was very flirtatious with lots of touching of both Dan and I. Dan announced he was going to bed as the drive and the alcohol had him on the verge of falling asleep in the chair, so off he went. Joanne and I stayed up for awhile and then started to clean up the after dinner mess. Joanne told me to go to bed and she would finish up and be right in.
